[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex, i'll kick off real quick. today we want to scope the poc around benchmark planning and integrating your scripts into our harness. jordan's here from SE to dig into perf and infra.
[00:00:42] Jordan (Redwood SE): hi all, Jordan. quick note, i'm going to ask for your canonical workload so we can run streaming and non-streaming tests. streaming tends to change the perf profile a bit because of chunking and tok gen overhead.
[00:01:20] Priya (SynthWave): yeah thanks. for context we're running a mix of short chat-like prompts (~20-40 tokens) and longer summarization jobs (~800-1200 tokens). our internal traffic is bursty — peak qps ~120, sustained ~30.
[00:01:55] Ben (SynthWave): and network wise we'll want VPC peering for Dedicated pilot, latency to us in east-1 is important. also need to confirm egress caps with infra.
[00:02:30] Elena (SynthWave CTO): top-line success for us is cost per active user at parity with our hosted infra and p95 latency < 600ms for short prompts. if that looks unrealistic we need to know tradeoffs.
[00:03:05] Alex (Redwood): great, that's helpful. jordan, can you talk through what our harness needs from them?
[00:03:30] Jordan (Redwood SE): sure — minimal: a script or small service that can call the model with sample payloads, plus a token distribution histogram or sample traces. we have a benchmark harness repo we'll share (GitHub link). the harness supports streaming and non-streaming modes and can replay traces at configurable qps.
[00:04:12] Priya (SynthWave): can the harness simulate user think time? our traffic has inter-request gaps.
[00:04:35] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes, we can do inter-arrival times, and we also have load patterns like constant, poisson, burst. we'll want representative traces so we don't over/under provision.
[00:05:10] Ben (SynthWave): what's the difference operationally between streaming and non-streaming tests for you?
[00:05:28] Jordan (Redwood SE): streaming keeps the connection open and emits tokens incrementally; it affects resource allocation because of longer-lived connections and impacts tail latency differently. non-streaming returns the full response at once and often has different batching behavior. for throughput math, streaming might reduce effective qps because of connection concurrency.
[00:06:01] Alex (Redwood): also important: caching behavior. our prefix/KV cache can help if you have repeated prefixes, but if each request is unique you won't see as much benefit. note i sometimes see transcripts where KV cache gets transcribed as K V cash in our internal notes, ha.
[00:06:28] Priya (SynthWave): ha, ok. For models, we're evaluating open models — Lama three variants and a couple quantized weights. we care about small model cost but quality must be acceptable.
[00:06:54] Jordan (Redwood SE): right; we'll run the same scripts across model variants and quantization profiles. we recommend starting with float16 and 8-bit quant, then try 4-bit if latency/cost targets require it. we'll also measure quality drift using your eval prompts.
[00:07:35] Elena (SynthWave CTO): on security, we need SOC2 and SSO/SAML details. Ben will own collecting those.
[00:07:48] Alex (Redwood): we'll share the security pack; Jordan can point to our Private deployment docs for VPC/on-prem notes.
[00:08:10] Ben (SynthWave): good. timeline expectations?
[00:08:22] Alex (Redwood): proposed: week 1 (2025-04-21) initial integration and microbenchmarks (non-streaming + streaming smoke tests). week 2 run 1-week load window on Dedicated pilot and gather metrics. post-run analyze cost/latency and a joint review.
[00:08:50] Priya (SynthWave): that aligns. we need to freeze the test scripts by 4/18.
[00:09:05] Jordan (Redwood SE): sounds good. on metrics we'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency, tail percentiles, error rates, tokens per request, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also capture GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates.
[00:09:32] Priya (SynthWave): about cost per 1k tokens — do you include infra overhead and network egress?
[00:09:45] Alex (Redwood): yes we can provide a cost breakdown: model compute, amortized infra, egress, and Redwood platform fee. for Dedicated pilots we can provide estimated commit pricing and a per-hour usage number for the test.
[00:10:12] Ben (SynthWave): for Dedicated, are there options to burst to hosted if we hit hot load? we want graceful degradation rather than failures.
[00:10:30] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes, routing policy can fallback to compatible hosted variants, and we can set an autoscale/burst policy. we'll document fallback latency and cost implications.
[00:10:52] Elena (SynthWave CTO): who will run the tests? our infra or redwood?
[00:11:00] Alex (Redwood): collaborative: you'll run your scripts via our harness in your account or in an isolated dedicated pilot environment we provision. Jordan will run the harness and produce the initial report; then we'll hand off to you to re-run if you want.
[00:11:28] Priya (SynthWave): about instrumentation — what logs/metrics do you need in the payload?
[00:11:40] Jordan (Redwood SE): just include request id and timestamp; the harness will add its own correlation ids. anonymize PII in payloads or provide synthetic data.
[00:11:58] Alex (Redwood): also, please include any eval prompts you use to measure quality so we can run regression checks across quant/float variants.
[00:12:18] Priya (SynthWave): we will. a question on streaming: our client opens 30 concurrent connections per host in production, will that map to 30 sessions on the runtime?
[00:12:35] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes roughly — each connection is a concurrent session; with streaming the memory footprint and KV cache life differ. we'll simulate those connection counts in the harness.
[00:13:00] Ben (SynthWave): any special network tuning needed for streaming?
[00:13:12] Jordan (Redwood SE): ensure keepalive settings and higher connection limits. we can provide recommended sysctl and nginx/gateway settings in the runbook.
[00:13:35] Alex (Redwood): i'm putting a note: we will also test fallback model variants to see quality/cost tradeoffs.
[00:13:44] Elena (SynthWave CTO): on success criteria — restating: p95 < 600ms for short prompts; cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll provide a target after a quick calc); no functional regression on eval set below our current threshold. if we hit p95 slightly above but cost savings are material we might accept it.
[00:14:10] Priya (SynthWave): what about synthetic vs real traces? we can provide both but real traces have some PII — synthetic will approximate.
[00:14:25] Jordan (Redwood SE): both are useful. synthetic + sampled real traces (PII removed) is ideal.
[00:14:50] Alex (Redwood): ok next, harness integration details: i'll send the repo link, it has a dockerized harness and a runner. you can either run it in your env or we'll schedule a run in the Dedicated pilot.
[00:15:20] Priya (SynthWave): if we run it in our env, do we need credentials to call redwood endpoints?
[00:15:32] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes we'll create a test API key with restricted scope and short TTL for the run. for private deployment we can do mutual TLS or KMS-backed auth.
[00:15:58] Ben (SynthWave): any concerns about tokenization differences across models when measuring tokens per request?
[00:16:08] Jordan (Redwood SE): good call — tokenizer differences matter. the harness will compute tokens with model-specific tokenizers and report both raw char-length and token count.
[00:16:35] Alex (Redwood): expected deliverables after the run: a raw metrics dump (csv/json), a summary dashboard, cost breakdown, and a short slide deck for the post-mortem.

[00:19:20] Priya (SynthWave): quick curious, have you had customers with a similar mix of short+long workloads? what tuning helped?
[00:19:30] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes — hybrid workloads often benefit from mixed routing: small requests to condensed models with aggressive batching; long jobs to higher-capacity instances and async workers. caching for repeated prompts and KV cache for conversation context can drastically lower token spend. quantization sometimes impacts quality on summarization tasks, so we run evals to ensure quality stays within bounds.
[00:20:05] Ben (SynthWave): for the Dedicated pilot, do you provide dedicated GPU types or is it shared?
[00:20:15] Alex (Redwood): Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — you pick instance families; we can provision a pilot with isolated capacity and configurable autoscale/burst.
[00:20:35] Priya (SynthWave): regarding model variants, we need to ensure our eval passes on the quantized small models; can you hook up eval runs to the harness?
[00:20:48] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes we have an eval runner that will run your prompts and compute the metrics you specify (ROUGE/BLEU/custom). we'll include regression alerting if quality drops beyond thresholds.
[00:21:20] Elena (SynthWave CTO): anything else on compliance?
[00:21:30] Alex (Redwood): we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, SAML SSO flow docs, and KMS integration notes. Ben wanted the retention config which we'll include.

[00:22:18] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes both time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token are measured; we also provide token emission rate graphs.

[00:24:15] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes, the post-run report will include recommended batching configs, quantization profiles, and model routing rules with expected cost/latency tradeoffs.
